edges.description: Mutant desmin incorporated into heteropolymers blocks normal assembly.
Failed assembly leaves the extrasarcomeric desmin network unable to form.
Misfolded desmin accumulates as granulofilamentous aggregates.
Loss of mechanical coupling destabilizes the myofibrillar apparatus.
Without desmin anchoring, mitochondria are mispositioned and damaged.
Aggregates overload and dysregulate the cell's protein quality-control systems.
Chronic proteostatic imbalance contributes to muscle-cell degeneration.
Mechanically vulnerable, disorganized myofibrils degenerate under contraction.
Bioenergetic failure contributes to muscle-cell degeneration.
Cardiomyocyte loss and remodeling produce cardiomyopathy.
Degeneration of conduction-system myocytes produces conduction disease.
Loss of skeletal muscle fibres produces distal-onset weakness.
Progressive fibre loss spreads to proximal muscles.
Diaphragmatic and intercostal involvement produces respiratory insufficiency.
Bulbar muscle involvement produces dysphagia in advanced disease.
Degenerating muscle fibres release creatine kinase into serum.
The cardiac insult manifests as cardiomyopathy.
Dilated cardiomyopathy is a common structural form.
Restrictive cardiomyopathy is the second most common structural form.
A hypertrophic form occurs in a minority.
An arrhythmogenic right-ventricular form occurs in a minority.
Progressive contractile dysfunction produces heart failure.
Remodeled, fibrotic myocardium is arrhythmogenic.
Ventricular arrhythmia can cause sudden cardiac death.
Conduction-system degeneration produces AV block.
Conduction block and arrhythmia can cause sudden cardiac death.
Network disruption increases myofibrillar mechanical vulnerability, as in human disease.
The mouse develops dilated cardiomyopathy, arrhythmias and conduction defects.
Null muscle shows architectural disruption and degeneration across muscle types.
